article_title: Buy Now, Securitize Later: BNPL's Growing Risks
news_headline: Klarna seeks U.S. bank charter in latest push beyond buy now, pay later
post_text:
On July 6, Klarna filed applications with the Utah Department of Financial Institutions and the FDIC to establish Klarna Bank USA, an FDIC-insured industrial bank. The Swedish BNPL giant serves 30 million Americans annually and has extended over $91.3 billion in U.S. credit since 2019, yet its stock sits at roughly half its $40 IPO price. A bank charter would let Klarna fund loans directly from customer deposits rather than expensive wholesale financing, cutting its dependence on third-party partner banks entirely.

This isn't just a corporate restructuring story. Twenty-four fintechs have filed for or received bank charters in the first half of 2026 alone. BNPL providers that once operated in the regulatory gaps between consumer lending and banking are now moving to occupy the full stack. The risk profile changes significantly when the same company originating installment credit also holds the deposits backing it.

A recent WBR piece on BNPL's growing systemic risks laid out exactly why that matters. The article examines how a lightly regulated, fast-scaling consumer credit market has been accumulating exposure that few are pricing in. Klarna's charter bid makes that argument harder to ignore. Read it on the WBR website.
